title: A superseded component digest is named in every service that pins it, and each service regenerates with the successor before the fail date
steps: With a fixture registry that holds a component at one digest, and three fixture service checkouts that pin that digest: the platform engineer changes the component, the registry publishes the new digest, and the platform engineer records it as the successor of the old digest with a fail date.
In one service checkout, the service author runs validate, and STEGO reports the superseded pin with its successor and fail date and does not fail.
The platform engineer names the old digest and the three checkouts, and STEGO names each service that pins it, with its version and digest.
In each checkout, the service author moves the pin to the successor, runs plan and then apply, and commits the diff with the record.
expected_result: Expects the sweep to name all three services and no other, and the time from the recorded supersession to the sweep to be inside 1 hour. Expects each service's committed record to pin the successor digest, with a date before the fail date, and each diff to change only the files the new digest affects.
notes: Not automated yet: ST-DIS-UC02, ST-DIS-UC04, ST-DIS-UC05 and ST-GEN-UC03 are not built yet, and the use case tests of ST-GEN-UC03 are not automated. Automate this test in the Go suite that the proof run runs when those use cases are built. A use case test of each step proves its use case; this test proves only that the steps take the fleet from the trigger to the result.
